acceptance_criteria.criterion: updateTitle(title) is a new public async method on LedgerStore
It reads the existing .meta.json, sets title, and updates last_updated
It returns the updated ProjectMeta object

summary: Added `updateTitle(title: string): Promise<ProjectMeta>` public async method to LedgerStore. The method reads the current .meta.json via readProjectMeta(), merges in the new title and a fresh last_updated timestamp, validates with ProjectMetaSchema.parse(), writes atomically via atomicWriteJson(this.metaPath(), updated), and returns the updated ProjectMeta. No new imports needed — atomicWriteJson and ProjectMetaSchema were already in scope. TypeScript type-check (tsc --noEmit) passed clean. All 1077 existing tests pass (36 test files).

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The method follows the same pattern as writeProjectMeta but is a targeted mutator that reads first and returns the validated result, which is the correct approach for a rename operation.

The plan's Risks section flags this as a potential race condition. writeRootIndexWithLock() uses proper locking; updateTitle() only relies on atomicWriteJson() for the write half. The WP-001 AC only required atomicWriteJson (met), but the Developer or Reviewer should decide whether to add withLock() wrapping before this ships. summary: Reviewed updateTitle(title: string): Promise<ProjectMeta> in mcp-server/src/storage/ledger-store.ts:295. All 6 acceptance criteria are met. Implementation is clean, minimal, and internally consistent with the codebase's established single-file meta write pattern (writeProjectMeta also does not use withLock for standalone writes — the lock is only applied at the multi-file level in writeRootIndexWithLock). The locking concern raised by QA is acknowledged: it is documented in the plan's Risks table and is a pre-ship decision, not a WP-001 blocker. No code changes required.

comments.note: The read-modify-write in updateTitle() runs without withLock(). Confirmed this is consistent with standalone writeProjectMeta() calls elsewhere in the class (e.g. initializeProject at line 173). The lock pattern in this codebase applies only to multi-file atomic operations (writeRootIndexWithLock). For a GUI rename endpoint with inherently low concurrency, atomicWriteJson is sufficient. Revisit if the method is ever called from a high-concurrency path. File: mcp-server/src/storage/ledger-store.ts:295.

Input validation (min(1) / max(200)) is intentionally deferred to the API layer (handleRenameProject in WP-002). The storage method accepts any string and ProjectMetaSchema would not reject an empty title (title is z.string().optional()). This is correct layering, but worth confirming that the API handler applies .min(1) as specced in the plan.
